subtopic: NaN / Inf detection and root-cause analysis
learningObjective: Diagnose the appearance of NaN in a Transformer forward pass using loss / activation statistics and localize the source op.
stem: In mid-training a 7B Transformer, loss becomes NaN at step 4213 after being stable for hundreds of prior steps. Activation-hook profiling records per-layer max-abs statistics as shown. Which diagnosis is best supported?
profileData:
Per-layer max(|activation|) at step 4212 (last healthy) vs step 4213 (NaN):
  layer 22 attn_scores:  before-softmax   step 4212 = 12.4       step 4213 = 27.8
  layer 22 attn_scores:  after-softmax    step 4212 = 0.94       step 4213 = NaN
  layer 22 attn_probs @ V                   step 4212 = 5.1        step 4213 = NaN (propagated)
  All prior layers (0-21):                                              finite in both steps
  Precision: fp16 activations, fp32 master weights, GradScaler enabled

options.text: The GradScaler failed to scale the loss and gradients underflowed to zero at step 4213; disabling GradScaler will fix the NaN because zero-gradient training is stable at any precision.

The attention scores at layer 22 exceeded FP16 range (max ≈ 65504) between steps 4212 and 4213, causing softmax input to overflow to Inf on one entry and produce NaN after normalization; typical fixes include upcasting attn_scores to FP32 before softmax (or using an implementation that fuses safe softmax with FP32 accumulator, e.g., FlashAttention).
Softmax over a vector with max ≈ 27.8 always overflows to Inf regardless of precision because exp(27.8) exceeds FP32 range; the fix is to switch entirely to FP64 for all training compute.
The NaN is a numerical fluke unrelated to the profile data; retraining from an earlier checkpoint with a different seed will always resolve NaN issues without changing precision or fusing softmax.

explanation: FP16 max is ~65504, and exp(27.8) ≈ 1.19e12 — well beyond FP16 range. In naive softmax implementations, an FP16 attention-score around 27+ causes exp(x) to overflow to +Inf, and the subsequent normalization produces NaN. The standard mitigation is to upcast the softmax to FP32 or use a FlashAttention-style safe softmax that subtracts the running max in higher precision. Option A misattributes to GradScaler. B is fatalistic. C falsely claims FP32 also overflows (exp(27.8) is only ~1e12, far under FP32 max ~3.4e38).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: GradScaler manages loss scaling; it does not gate attention-score overflow.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: FP16 range + exp of large logit is a classic overflow-to-NaN pattern.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: root-cause is diagnosable and fixable.

assumptions: Naive softmax (no safe-softmax max-subtract) at FP16.
The profile data reflects genuine max-abs activation statistics.
nonImplications: Does not imply FlashAttention is required; any safe-softmax variant with FP32 accum works.
Does not imply FP16 training is doomed; safe softmax + gradient clipping is sufficient in most cases.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses gradient scaling with forward overflow.
